key_insight: Thermal history, along with composition, controls hidden local octahedral-tilt nanodomains in lead halide perovskites, which in turn alter their optoelectronic response.
engineering_relevance: Perovskite device performance and stability depend not only on chemistry but also on processing thermal ramps, making heat history a design variable for fabrication and operating conditions.
method: Single-crystal X-ray and neutron diffuse scattering across Cs/MA/FA and Cl/Br/I compositions
Machine-learning-assisted molecular dynamics plus a phenomenological octahedral-tilt model
Hyperspectral photoluminescence across phase transitions and thermal ramp rates
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent observation of equilibrium dynamic nanodomains in nearly every composition and a heating-rate-dependent change in MAPbI3 photoluminescence quantum efficiency across a phase transition.
watch_item: Because the effect depends on phase transitions within device-relevant temperature ranges, processing and operating thermal profiles must be tightly controlled to avoid unintentional performance shifts.
paper_title: Thermal history controls the optoelectronic response of lead halide perovskites through structure and dynamics
